How to make a proper bedroll step by step

Practical tips from real-world field experience

snippet.title: BOOMING, but the Power Grid is FAILING! & Largest Expat Meet Up Ever
snippet.description:
It has been a rough time here in Roxas City. Laura and I have been dealing with severe power outages affecting the entire Western Visayas grid. With constant yellow and red alerts, we are essentially at 100% capacity, meaning rolling blackouts, running the generator constantly, and getting absolutely no sleep. The region is experiencing massive growth with new resorts and condos going up constantly, but the power infrastructure just isn't keeping up. I think we are all going to need to adopt solar power very soon!

Despite the grid issues, we hosted our busiest expat meetup yet at the Canadian Beaver! It happens on the second Sunday of every month, and we had so many friends show up that we completely ran out of tables. Even with the lightning, thunder, and rain, the turnout was absolutely amazing.


I created a FREE Website to help people figure out where the best places to live in the Philippines are for their personality, as well a resource guide where to get everything you need before making the move to the Philippines.

snippet.title: The 10 States That Are Most Likely to Face Blackouts in 2026
snippet.description:
🎁 🚩💡🔗 Get the FREE guide: How to turn $50 into a 90-day food supply → https://zachofalltrades.io/freeplan/


The U.S. power grid is facing unprecedented threats in 2025, and eleven states are at the highest risk for major blackouts.


 
n this comprehensive analysis, I break down exactly which states are most vulnerable—Michigan, Louisiana, Illinois, Massachusetts, New York, Florida, Arizona, North Carolina, Texas, and California, and reveal the converging factors putting our electrical infrastructure at the breaking point.



From aging 1960s-era infrastructure to extreme weather events, from renewable energy transition challenges to explosive electricity demand from EVs and data centers, the North American grid is operating on borrowed time. 



The Department of Energy warns that blackouts could increase by 100 times by 2030, and the North American Electric Reliability Corporation shows most of the U.S. at elevated risk for electricity shortfalls.



I examine state-by-state vulnerabilities: Michigan's polar vortex risks and EV manufacturing electricity demands, Louisiana's hurricane-prone infrastructure, Illinois's dependency on retiring nuclear plants, Massachusetts's LNG supply chain issues, New York's maxed-out transmission system, Florida's explosive population growth, Arizona's extreme heat challenges with the Palo Verde nuclear plant, North Carolina's pipeline capacity problems and physical security threats, Texas's isolated ERCOT grid and February 2021 collapse lessons, and California's wildfire preemptive shutoffs and the infamous duck curve problem.




Beyond individual state risks, I cover the national threats affecting everyone: cascading failure potential across interconnected grids, accelerating climate change impacts, the cybersecurity nightmare with nation-state actors already inside our systems, the joke that is physical grid security with 55,000+ vulnerable substations, and the simultaneous explosion in electricity demand from electric vehicles, AI data centers, and cryptocurrency mining.





Most importantly, I provide actionable preparation strategies you can implement now: backup power solutions, solar and battery systems, food and water security, medical preparedness, communication plans, financial readiness with cash reserves, community resilience building, physical security considerations, and practical skills that don't require electricity.



This isn't fear-mongering, it's pattern recognition based on official reports, utility insider knowledge, and infrastructure assessments. 


The grid was built for a world that no longer exists, and we're not adapting fast enough to prevent major failures.

snippet.title: Hundreds of residents evacuated after deadly wildfires in Spain  | BBC News
snippet.description:
At least 12 people have died in a wildfire in southern Spain, with early indications suggesting four of the victims are British, according to a local official.

Hundreds of emergency responders are working to contain the blaze around Los Gallardos, Almería, which appears to have been caused by a downed power line.

The bodies of the victims were found near the small village of Bédar, just outside Los Gallardos, while 23 others are still missing and hundreds of residents have been evacuated.

snippet.title: 7.7 EARTHQUAKE ROCKS PANAMA — Tonosí Cut Off as Buildings Collapse (Live Updates)
snippet.description:
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck central Panama on October 9, 2026, damaging buildings, splitting roads and triggering tsunami warnings across parts of the Pacific. The shaking was felt in Panama City and neighboring Colombia, while repeated aftershocks sent residents back outside and complicated emergency response efforts.

Penonomé suffered major damage, including the collapse of a cathedral bell tower. Historic structures in Los Santos were also affected, power outages hit six provinces, and Tocumen International Airport temporarily suspended operations. The tsunami alerts were later lifted, but seawater reached homes on Isla Cañas, and the town of Tonosí remained cut off by damaged roads.

In this video... we examine the earthquake's impact, the communities isolated by highway damage, the emergency response, and the fault system scientists identified beneath southern Panama.

Authorities reported injuries but no documented deaths as of Friday evening, while warning that the situation could change as teams reached more affected areas. The Panama Canal continued operating normally, even as officials assessed potential economic losses and international partners offered assistance.

Aftershocks continued into Saturday, October 10, with schools suspended nationwide and residents facing uncertainty about damaged homes and infrastructure. With a national evacuation drill scheduled for Monday, the disaster has become an immediate test of Panama's earthquake preparedness.

What would you do if your home suddenly lost power for 3 days? In Japan, where earthquakes, typhoons, and other disasters can cause extended outages, emergency preparedness has become an important part of everyday life.

In this video, we explore the $40 emergency power and blackout kit inspired by practical Japanese disaster-preparedness habits. From lighting and phone charging to essential household needs, you'll discover how a relatively inexpensive kit can help keep your family prepared when the electricity goes out.

• How Japanese households prepare for extended power outages

• Essential items to keep ready before an emergency happens
• Common preparedness mistakes to avoid

• Why preparation matters during earthquakes, storms, and other disasters

Whether you're preparing for a winter storm, hurricane, earthquake, or unexpected blackout, these simple preparedness ideas can help you stay safer and more comfortable when the power goes down.
